s: Who are the main beneficiaries of ICDS?
o: Children aged 6–14 years and pregnant women
Children aged six months to six years, pregnant women and lactating mothers
Pregnant women and lactating mothers only
x: ICDS primarily covers children from six months to six years, pregnant women and lactating mothers.

s: Through which institution is Supplementary Nutrition delivered under ICDS?
x: Supplementary Nutrition is delivered through the Anganwadi Centre, while immunisation, health check-up and referral go through the health system.

s: Under which scheme is ICDS now run as Anganwadi Services?
x: ICDS, a centrally sponsored MWCD scheme implemented by States/UTs, now runs as Anganwadi Services under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0.

s: Which of the following is NOT included among the six ICDS services?
x: Cash maternity benefit is provided under PMMVY, now associated with Mission Shakti, and is not one of the six ICDS services.

s: On which date was the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme launched?
x: ICDS was launched on 2 October 1975 and universalised in 2006.

s: Which is the nodal ministry for ICDS?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
x: ICDS is run by MWCD; PM POSHAN is under the Ministry of Education.

s: Who among the following runs the Anganwadi Centre as the honorary grassroots functionary of ICDS?
x: The Anganwadi Worker is the honorary grassroots ICDS functionary who runs the centre; ANM and ASHA belong to the NHM.

s: Which of the following functionaries belongs to the National Health Mission and not to ICDS?
x: ASHA and ANM are NHM health workers; Anganwadi Workers, Helpers and CDPOs are ICDS functionaries.

s: Under ICDS, through which system are immunisation, health check-up and referral services delivered?
x: Three ICDS services - immunisation, health check-up and referral - come through the health system, showing convergence of the Health and WCD ministries.

s: Which institute trains the Child Development Project Officers (CDPOs) of the ICDS programme?
x: The National Institute of Public Cooperation and Child Development (NIPCCD) trains CDPOs, the block-level ICDS officers.

s: Who is the block-level officer of the ICDS programme?
x: The CDPO is the block-level ICDS officer; NIPCCD trains CDPOs.

s: As per AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, how many ICDS projects are there in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh has 55,746 Anganwadi Centres in 257 ICDS projects.

s: As ICDS completed 50 years in 2025, about how many Anganwadi Centres were there in India?
x: At 50 years, ICDS had about 1.4 million (14 lakh) Anganwadi Centres; 55,746 is the AP figure.

s: In which year was the ICDS scheme universalised?
x: ICDS, launched on 2 October 1975, was universalised in 2006.

s: One Nation One Anganwadi mainly lets which group keep ICDS benefits?
o: Adolescent girls in the North-East only
Families holding a child's Aadhaar only
Migrant families moving to another State
x: It lets migrant families keep ICDS benefits for children below six and pregnant/lactating women in another State; child Aadhaar is not mandatory.

s:
Arrange in chronological order:
A. Launch of ICDS
B. Universalisation of ICDS
C. Introduction of the Mid-Day Meal Scheme
D. Introduction of Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0
x: ICDS was launched in 1975, the Mid-Day Meal Scheme came in 1995, ICDS was universalised in 2006, and Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 was introduced in 2021.

s: What does the foundational stage under the National Education Policy, 2020 comprise?
o: Ages 3–6, excluding the first two years of school
Ages 3–8, including three years of Anganwadi/pre-school and Classes 1–2
x: The NEP 2020 foundational stage covers ages 3–8: three years of Anganwadi or preschool followed by Classes 1 and 2.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years?
x: Article 45 provides for ECCE for children up to six years. Article 21A is the right to education for 6-14 years; Article 39(f) concerns healthy development of children as a directive; Article 51A(k) is the parents' fundamental duty to provide education opportunities to children aged 6-14.

s: In which year was the National Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) Policy adopted?
x: The National ECCE Policy dates from 2013; NEP 2020 created the foundational stage.

s: What is the main aim of Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi?
o: Provide one hot cooked meal to children in Classes I–VIII
Provide cash maternity benefit to pregnant women
Bring early childhood care and education into Anganwadis through play-based pedagogy
Provide take-home ration to adolescent girls
x: Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi integrates ECCE into Anganwadis and promotes play-based pedagogy, effectively developing them as pre-schools.

s: The Scheme for Adolescent Girls under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 covers which group?
o: Girls aged 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern Region
All boys and girls aged 6-14 years
Girls aged 10-14 years in all districts
Girls aged 15-19 years only in urban areas
x: The Scheme for Adolescent Girls covers girls aged 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern Region.

s: Which of the following was NOT merged into Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (2021)?
x: PM POSHAN is a separate school-meal scheme; Poshan 2.0 merged Anganwadi Services/SNP, POSHAN Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls.

s: In which year was Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 introduced?
x: Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 began in 2021 under MWCD as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.

s: Under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, what is the Centre-State funding ratio for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and J&K?
x: NE and Himalayan States and J&K get 90:10; general States 60:40; UTs without legislature are 100% Centre.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three verticals of Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0?
x: The three verticals are nutrition support, ECCE (3-6 years) and Anganwadi infrastructure; school meals are under PM POSHAN.

s: Under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, Early Childhood Care and Education is meant for children of which age group?
x: The ECCE vertical of Poshan 2.0 covers children aged 3-6 years.

s: How many Anganwadi Centres are to be upgraded as Saksham Anganwadis at the rate of 40,000 a year?
x: 2 lakh AWCs are to be upgraded as Saksham Anganwadis at 40,000 a year.

s: How long does the Poshan Pakhwada nutrition campaign last?
x: Poshan Pakhwada is a fortnight-long campaign; its 8th edition (2026) focused on brain development in the first six years.

s: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on which occasion and at which place?
x: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on 8 March 2018 at Jhunjhunu in Rajasthan.

s: To what level did POSHAN Abhiyaan aim to reduce stunting by 2022?
x: POSHAN Abhiyaan aimed to reduce stunting to 25% by 2022, as part of a Jan Andolan for a Suposhit Bharat.

s: What does Poshan Vatika refer to?
x: Poshan Vatikas are nutrition gardens at Anganwadi centres; play-based ECCE is Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi.

s: Which of the following portal–function pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: PMMVY Soft Portal – DBT verification and cash benefits for pregnant and lactating mothers
Poshan Tracker App – Panic-button distress dispatch
x: Poshan Tracker monitors nutrition and Anganwadi services in real time; panic-button dispatch is 112 India.

s: In which month is Rashtriya Poshan Maah observed every year?
x: Poshan Maah is in September; Poshan Pakhwada is a fortnight in March–April.

s: Where was the 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah (2026) held?
x: The 9th Poshan Maah (2026) was at Varanasi; POSHAN Abhiyaan began at Jhunjhunu and BBBP at Panipat.

s: The 112 India App is associated with which of the following functions?
o: Unified single-number panic-button response with police, medical and fire dispatch
Online registration for SC students in private residential schools
Direct benefit transfer for pregnant and lactating mothers
Digital profiling of sewer and septic tank workers
x: The 112 India app (ERSS) is a single-number panic button that sends police, ambulance or fire services, with special routing for women's safety.

s: Which edition of Rashtriya Poshan Maah was held at Varanasi in 2026?
x: The 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah (September 2026) was held at Varanasi with the theme 'Hamari Anganwadi Hamari Jimmedari'.

s: Which edition of Poshan Pakhwada was held in April 2026 with a focus on brain development in the first six years?
x: The 8th Poshan Pakhwada (April 2026) focused on brain development in the first six years.

s: What is the full form of POSHAN in POSHAN Abhiyaan?
o: Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment
Prime Minister's Organised Scheme for Health and Nutrition
Programme for Overall Support to Health and Nutrition
x: POSHAN Abhiyaan is the Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment, earlier the National Nutrition Mission.

s: What is the goal of POSHAN Abhiyaan, which is run as a Jan Andolan?
x: POSHAN Abhiyaan aims at a Suposhit (well-nourished) Bharat through a Jan Andolan.

s: Which is the nodal ministry for PM POSHAN, the renamed Mid-Day Meal Scheme?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
x: PM POSHAN is run by the Ministry of Education (Department of School Education and Literacy); MWCD runs ICDS.

s: PM POSHAN is implemented as a rights-based Centrally Sponsored Scheme under which legislation?
x: PM POSHAN is a rights-based Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented under the National Food Security Act, 2013.

s: Besides better nutrition, what does PM POSHAN aim to tackle?
x: PM POSHAN aims to address classroom hunger and raise enrolment, attendance, retention and concentration.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of PM POSHAN?
o: Participation of Farmer Producer Organisations and Self-Help Groups
Additional nutrition in aspirational and high-anaemia districts
Social audit only in selected districts on an optional basis
x: Under PM POSHAN, social audit is mandatory in every district, not optional.

s: The Mid-Day Meal Scheme was introduced on 15 August 1995 under which name?
o: National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education
x: The scheme was introduced on 15 August 1995 as the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE).

s: Tithi Bhojan, associated with community participation in PM POSHAN, was first introduced by which State?
x: Tithi Bhojan, under which communities contribute meals on special occasions, was first introduced by Gujarat.

s: Which classes are covered under PM POSHAN?
o: Bal Vatika and Classes I to VIII
x: PM POSHAN gives one hot cooked meal to Bal Vatika and Classes I–VIII in government and aided schools.

s: What is the nutritional norm per child at the primary level under PM POSHAN?
x: Primary: 450 kcal and 12 g protein; upper primary: 700 kcal and 20 g protein.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Akshaya Patra Foundation—largest NGO partner in the mid-day meal programme
Tithi Bhojan—introduced first by Tamil Nadu
PM POSHAN—administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: The Akshaya Patra Foundation, based in Bengaluru, is identified as the largest NGO partner in the mid-day meal programme. The other pairings contain incorrect State, Ministry or year associations.

s: Which State first introduced the mid-day meal?
x: Tamil Nadu was first with the mid-day meal; Gujarat was first with Tithi Bhojan.

s: In which year was the Mid-Day Meal Scheme renamed PM POSHAN?
x: It was renamed PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman) in 2021.

s: In 2024-25, to which classes was Andhra Pradesh's Dokka Seethamma Mid-Day Meal extended?
x: AP extended the Dokka Seethamma Mid-Day Meal to Intermediate (Classes 11–12) in 2024-25.

s: In what ratio do the Centre and the States share the cost of PM POSHAN?
x: PM POSHAN, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Ministry of Education, is shared 60:40 between the Centre and States.

s: What is the full form of PM POSHAN?
o: Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment
x: The Mid-Day Meal Scheme was renamed PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman) in 2021.

s: What is the nutritional norm per child at the upper primary level under PM POSHAN?
x: Upper primary children get 700 kcal and 20 g protein; primary children get 450 kcal and 12 g.

s: Where is the Akshaya Patra Foundation, the largest NGO mid-day meal provider, based?
x: Akshaya Patra Foundation was founded in Bengaluru in 2000 by Madhu Pandit Dasa.

s: Which provision is the legal basis of the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana?
o: Section 4 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013
x: PMMVY has its legal basis in Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013.

s: Under which framework and ministry was Janani Suraksha Yojana launched in 2005?
o: National Food Security Act and Ministry of Women and Child Development
Samarthya and Ministry of Women and Child Development
Mission Vatsalya and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
National Rural Health Mission and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: JSY was launched in 2005 under the National Rural Health Mission and is administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. It is a 100% Centrally Sponsored Scheme.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its nodal ministry?
o: JSSK — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
PMSMA — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
JSY — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
PMMVY — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: PMMVY is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development. JSY, JSSK and PMSMA are associated with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

s: What does Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) entitle pregnant women and sick newborns to?
o: A cash incentive for institutional delivery
Free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport
Rs 5,000 maternity benefit for the first child
A free antenatal check-up on the 9th of every month
x: JSSK, launched in 2011 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides pregnant women and sick newborns free delivery, medicines, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport.

s: Under PMMVY 2.0 (from April 2022), which of the following correctly describes the maternity benefit?
o: Rs 5,000 for the first child, and Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl
Rs 5,000 in three instalments for the first two children irrespective of sex
Rs 6,000 for every live birth irrespective of birth order
Rs 1,400 for institutional delivery in rural areas
x: PMMVY 2.0 gives Rs 5,000 for the first child and Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl. Rs 5,000 in three instalments was the old PMMVY 1.0 design (a trap). It does not cover every birth. Rs 1,400 for rural institutional delivery is the JSY benefit.

s: Under Janani Suraksha Yojana, what is the cash assistance for institutional delivery in rural areas?
x: JSY gives ₹1,400 in rural and ₹1,000 in urban areas; ₹500 is for home delivery for BPL women.

s: Which of the following scheme–benefit pairs is correctly matched?
o: JSSK – Breastfeeding within one hour of birth
PMSMA – Free antenatal check-up on the 9th of every month
JSY – ₹6,000 if the second child is a girl
x: PMSMA gives free antenatal check-ups on the 9th of every month; MAA is breastfeeding, JSY is institutional-delivery cash and ₹6,000 is PMMVY.

s: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan is associated with which of the following?
o: Promotion of breastfeeding within one hour of birth
Free treatment exclusively for sick newborns
Free antenatal check-up on the ninth of every month and identification of high-risk pregnancies
Cash assistance for institutional delivery at rural and urban rates
x: PMSMA, launched in 2016 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides free antenatal check-ups on the 9th of every month and helps identify high-risk pregnancies.

s: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) launched?
x: PMSMA was launched in 2016 by the Health Ministry to give free antenatal check-ups on the 9th of every month.

s: What does the MAA (Mothers' Absolute Affection) programme promote?
o: Breastfeeding within one hour of birth
Cash benefit for the first child
x: MAA (2016, Health Ministry) promotes breastfeeding, starting within one hour of birth.

s: In which year was Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) launched?
x: JSSK, of the Health Ministry, began in 2011; JSY began in 2005 and PMSMA in 2016.

s: From which date was the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) implemented?
x: PMMVY of the MWCD has run from 1 January 2017.

s: What is the tagline of the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana?
x: PMMVY's tagline is 'Matru Shakti Rashtra Shakti'.

s: Palna, the National Creche Scheme, is intended for children in which age group?
x: Palna covers children from 6 months to 6 years. Its creches may function whether or not the mother is employed, and 17,000 Anganwadi-cum-Creches were targeted.

s: Under which mission has CHILDLINE 1098 been integrated with ERSS-112 in 36 States and Union Territories?
x: Under Mission Vatsalya, CHILDLINE 1098 has been integrated with ERSS-112 in 36 States and Union Territories.

s: Which scheme did Mission Vatsalya, introduced in 2021-22, subsume?
x: Mission Vatsalya subsumed the Integrated Child Protection Scheme, or ICPS.

s: Under Mission Vatsalya, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: JJB and CWC — One in every State only
Sponsorship and foster care — Rs.4,000 per child per month
Institutional care — Rs.4,000 per child per month
Aftercare — Available only up to 18 years
x: Mission Vatsalya provides Rs.4,000 per child per month for non-institutional care through sponsorship and foster care. JJBs and CWCs are to be established in every district; institutional care is Rs.3,000 per month and aftercare extends beyond 18 years.

s: What corpus does PM CARES for Children give eligible COVID-19 orphaned children at the age of 23?
x: PM CARES for Children (2021), for children who lost parents or guardians to COVID-19, provides a corpus of Rs 10 lakh at 23 along with education and health support.

s: Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Amendment Act, 2021, who has been made the focal point for adoption matters in a district?
x: The JJ Amendment Act 2021 made the District Magistrate the focal point for adoption. The CWC is a statutory body for children in need of care, but not the designated focal point; the District Judge and SP are not given this role.

s: Which age group is covered by aftercare support under Mission Vatsalya?
x: Aftercare covers 18–21 (extendable to 23) at ₹4,000 a month.

s:
Consider the following statements about child support schemes:
1. Under Mission Vatsalya, sponsorship and foster care support is ₹4,000 per child per month.
2. Palna creches are open only to children of employed mothers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Palna is open whether or not the mother is employed.

s: What is the total outlay of Mission Vatsalya for 2021-22 to 2025-26?
x: Mission Vatsalya's outlay is Rs 10,916 crore, of which the Centre's share is Rs 6,928 crore.

s: Which body first started creches for the children of working mothers in India?
x: The Central Social Welfare Board started the first creches; this led to the Rajiv Gandhi National Creche Scheme and then Palna.

s: Which is the nodal ministry for Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
x: MWCD is nodal for BBBP, working with Health and Education; the Finance Ministry runs Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana.

s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched at which place on 22 January 2015?
x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched on 22 January 2015 at Panipat in Haryana.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: It is primarily a behaviour-change campaign
It provides direct benefit transfers to every girl child
Funds for each district vary with its Sex Ratio at Birth
x: BBBP has no DBT component; it is a behaviour-change campaign with no asset creation.

s: Which of the following scheme–feature pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Balika Samriddhi Yojana – Cash grant at birth and scholarships for girls of BPL families
Dhanalakshmi – Conditional cash transfer linked with birth registration, immunisation and schooling
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao – Behaviour-change campaign for survival and education of the girl child
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana – Savings scheme with maturity at 15 years
x: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana matures at 21 years, not 15.

s: After how many years does a Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana account mature?
x: SSY, under the Ministry of Finance, allows up to two girls per family, deposits of ₹250 to ₹1.5 lakh a year, and matures at 21 years.

s: In which year was Dhanalakshmi, a pilot conditional cash transfer for the girl child, launched?
x: Dhanalakshmi began in 2008; Balika Samriddhi Yojana dates from 1997.

s: Which Ministry runs the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (2015) is a small-savings scheme of the Ministry of Finance for up to two girls.

s: In which year was the Balika Samriddhi Yojana for girls of BPL families launched?
x: Balika Samriddhi Yojana (1997) gives a cash grant at birth and scholarships to BPL girls.

s: Under Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, the sex ratio at birth improved from 918 to what figure?
x: The sex ratio at birth rose from 918 to 929.

s: For how many girls in a family can Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana accounts be opened?
x: Sukanya Samriddhi accounts can be opened for up to two girls.

s: What is the minimum annual deposit under Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana?
x: Deposits range from Rs 250 to Rs 1.5 lakh a year, for 15 years.

s: On 1 July 2026, the Allahabad High Court held that the age limits under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act apply:
o: Only to persons not governed by personal laws
To all citizens irrespective of religion
Only to residents of Uttar Pradesh
x: The Allahabad High Court held that the PCMA age limits apply to all citizens irrespective of religion.

s: What is the minimum legal age of marriage under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006?
o: 21 years for both girls and boys
18 years for girls and 21 years for boys
18 years for girls and 18 years for boys
21 years for girls and 18 years for boys
x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 prescribes 18 years for girls and 21 years for boys.

s: What is the punishment for an adult male who contracts, conducts or promotes a child marriage under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006?
o: Rigorous imprisonment up to two years and fine up to Rs. 1 lakh
Fine up to Rs. 10 lakh only
Simple imprisonment up to five years without fine
Imprisonment up to one year and fine up to Rs. 50,000
x: The punishment may extend to two years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine up to Rs. 1 lakh.

s: The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021 proposed to raise the minimum marriageable age of women to 21 years. What happened to the Bill?
o: It was withdrawn after being passed by both Houses.
It was rejected by the Supreme Court.
It was enacted as an Act in 2022.
It was referred to a Standing Committee and lapsed with the 17th Lok Sabha.
x: The Bill was sent to a Standing Committee and subsequently lapsed with the 17th Lok Sabha.

s: What is the legal status of a child marriage under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006?
o: Void ab initio in all cases
Voidable at the option of the party who was a minor at the time of marriage
Voidable only at the option of the State Government
x: Under PCMA 2006 a child marriage is voidable at the option of the minor party, not automatically void. It is not fully valid and unchallengeable, and the option lies with the minor party, not the State Government.

s: Who appoints Child Marriage Prohibition Officers under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006?
x: Child Marriage Prohibition Officers are appointed by State Governments.

s: According to NFHS-5, which State has the highest share of women aged 20–24 married before 18?
x: NFHS-5 shows 23.3% nationally, with West Bengal the highest.

s: ALIVA, a data-driven model to end child marriage, was developed in which district?
x: ALIVA is the child-marriage-free model of Nayagarh district in Odisha.

s: As per NFHS-5, what share of women aged 20-24 were married before the age of 18?
x: NFHS-5 shows 23.3% of women aged 20-24 married before 18, highest in West Bengal.

s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) is presently implemented under which component of Mission Shakti?
x: BBBP is implemented under Sambal, the safety component of Mission Shakti.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the PMMVY Soft Portal is incorrect?
o: It is a portal for employment listings for Divyangjan.
It is associated with the Ministry of Women & Child Development.
It facilitates cash benefit payout for pregnant and lactating mothers.
It supports Direct Benefit Transfer verification.
x: Option A is incorrect: job listings for Divyangjan are on PM-DAKSH. The PMMVY portal (WCD) verifies DBT and pays cash benefits to pregnant and breastfeeding mothers.

s: Which scheme is described as one of the world’s largest SHG-based rural livelihood programmes?
x: DAY-NRLM, launched in 2011, is an SHG-based rural livelihoods programme described as one of the world’s largest.

s: Of which scheme is Swadhar, which gives shelter to women in difficult circumstances, now a part?
x: Swadhar now sits inside Shakti Sadan; Ujjawala deals with trafficking and PMUY (MoPNG) gives LPG connections.

s: Shakti Sadan under Mission Shakti – Samarthya combines which two schemes?
x: Shakti Sadan merges Ujjawala and Swadhar; Palna and PMMVY are separate Samarthya components.

s: What does Rashtriya Mahila Kosh, set up in 1993, provide?
o: Shelter for women in difficult circumstances
Micro-credit to poor women without collateral
x: RMK gives collateral-free micro-credit to poor women in the informal sector.

s: What does the Ujjawala scheme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development deal with?
x: Ujjawala is about trafficking; PM Ujjwala Yojana (MoPNG) gives LPG connections.

s:
Assertion (A): The SHe-Box Portal is a centralized platform for workplace sexual-harassment complaints.
Reason (R): It registers and monitors complaints under the POSH Act.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
