s: Which of the following is NOT an umbrella mission of the Ministry of Women and Child Development?
x: MWCD schemes are grouped under three umbrella missions - Poshan 2.0, Shakti and Vatsalya; Mission Indradhanush is an immunisation drive of the Health Ministry.

s: Which are the two sub-schemes of Mission Shakti of the Ministry of Women and Child Development?
x: Mission Shakti has Sambal (safety, including BBBP) and Samarthya (empowerment, including Shakti Sadan, Palna and PMMVY).

s: Which Ministry runs the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, which gives deposit-free LPG connections to women of poor households?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: PM Ujjwala (May 2016) is run by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas; Ujjawala (trafficking) is an MWCD scheme.

s: What is the full form of DWCRA?
o: Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas
Department of Women and Child Rights Administration
Development of Working Children in Rural Areas
District Women and Child Resource Agency
x: DWCRA means Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas (1982).

s: In which year was DWCRA (Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas) launched?
x: DWCRA began in 1982; Rashtriya Mahila Kosh came in 1993 and DAY-NRLM in 2011.

s: What does Swavalambini (2022), a programme of MSDE and NITI Aayog, promote?
o: Entrepreneurship among women students in the North-East
Shelter for women in difficult circumstances
x: Swavalambini promotes entrepreneurship among women students in the North-East.

s: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana launched?
x: PM Ujjwala Yojana of MoPNG was launched in May 2016.

s: From March 2026, what is the subsidy per LPG cylinder under PM Ujjwala Yojana?
x: The subsidy is Rs 300 per cylinder for up to 12 refills (8 March 2026; earlier Rs 200).

s: According to NFHS-5 (2019-21), what is the level of stunting among children under five in India?
x: Stunting fell from 38.4% (NFHS-4) to 35.5% (NFHS-5); 19.3% is wasting and 32.1% underweight.

s: What was India's rank in the Global Hunger Index 2025?
x: India was 102nd of 123 (score 25.8, 'serious') in 2025, up from 105th in 2024.

s: According to NFHS-5, what is the level of anaemia among women aged 15-49?
x: Anaemia in women aged 15–49 is 57.0% in NFHS-5.

s:
Consider the following statements about NFHS-5 (2019-21) indicators for children under five:
1. Wasting in India is 19.3%.
2. Underweight in Andhra Pradesh is higher than the national figure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP underweight is 29.6% against India's 32.1%.

s: Which programme targets anaemia, a leading cause of maternal deaths in India?
x: Anaemia Mukt Bharat is aimed at reducing anaemia, which affects 57% of women aged 15-49 (NFHS-5).

s: The under-five mortality rate counts deaths of children before which age, per 1,000 live births?
x: U5MR counts deaths before the 5th birthday; IMR counts deaths before age 1.

s: According to NFHS-5, what is the level of stunting among children under five in Andhra Pradesh?
x: NFHS-5 stunting is 31.2% in AP against 35.5% for India.

s: In the Global Hunger Index 2025, in which category was India's level of hunger placed?
x: India ranked 102nd of 123 with a score of 25.8, in the 'serious' category.

s: On which date was YSR Sampoorna Poshana launched in Andhra Pradesh?
x: It was launched on 7 Sept 2020 for pregnant and lactating women and children 6–72 months.

s: To which age group of children does Balamrutham in Andhra Pradesh give take-home ration?
x: Balamrutham is take-home ration for children 6 months–3 years.

s: Where is YSR Sampoorna Poshana Plus implemented?
x: Sampoorna Poshana Plus covers 77 tribal mandals (8,320 AWCs).

s:
Match the following Andhra Pradesh schemes with their purpose:
List-I
A. YSR Sampoorna Poshana
B. Balamrutham
C. Dokka Seethamma
List-II
1. Mid-day meal in schools
2. Take-home ration for children 6 months-3 years
3. Nutritious food for pregnant and lactating women and children 6-72 months
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Sampoorna Poshana feeds mothers and children 6-72 months, Balamrutham is take-home ration for 6 months-3 years, and Dokka Seethamma is the school mid-day meal.

s: With what is Anna Amrutha Hastham of Andhra Pradesh associated?
o: Free bus travel for persons with disabilities
x: Anna Amrutha Hastham is an earlier Anganwadi nutrition scheme continued alongside YSR Sampoorna Poshana.

s: The Accessible India Campaign was launched on which date?
x: The Accessible India Campaign was launched on 3 December 2015 as a flagship initiative for universal accessibility.

s: What is the Sugamya Bharat App mainly used for?
o: Providing monthly pensions to persons with disabilities
x: The Sugamya Bharat App functions as a crowdsourcing platform through which accessibility gaps can be reported.

s: Built environment and transport are two verticals of the Accessible India Campaign. Which is the third?
x: The verticals are built environment, transport and ICT; accessible booths and Braille-enabled EVMs are accessible-election measures, not a vertical.

s: By what other name is the Accessible India Campaign known?
x: The Accessible India Campaign is also called Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan. It was launched on 3 December 2015 as the flagship of DEPwD.

s: With which of the following is the UDID Portal (Swavlamban) mainly associated?
o: Centralized issuing of Unique Disability IDs and digital disability certificates
Online digital library for accessible books
Digital profiling of sewer and septic tank workers
Online registration for private residential schools
x: The UDID portal (Swavlamban), under DEPwD, issues Unique Disability IDs and digital disability certificates from one place, so benefits are easy to get.

s: Through which app is school-based screening of children for 21 disabilities done?
x: PRASHAST is the screening app; the Sugamya Bharat App takes accessibility complaints.

s:
Assertion (A): Sugamya Pustakalaya delivers online books in accessible formats.
Reason (R): Its formats include DAISY, audio, and Braille.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: Sugamya Pustakalaya offers accessible books online because it holds them in DAISY, audio and Braille formats. R explains A.

s: Which of the following is an accessible-elections measure for persons with disabilities?
x: Accessible elections include accessible polling booths and Braille-enabled EVMs.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about disability portals and apps?
o: The UDID Portal comes under DEPwD
The PM-DAKSH Portal comes under DEPwD
The PRASHAST App comes under DEPwD
The Accessible India Campaign is a DEPwD flagship
x: PRASHAST comes under Education (NCERT/DoSEL), not DEPwD; UDID and PM-DAKSH are DEPwD.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: UDID — single national disability ID and certificate
SIPDA — monthly pension to BPL households
x: UDID provides a single national disability identity and certificate. SIPDA, DDRS and PM-DAKSH have different functions.

s: Which scheme provides free aids and appliances to eligible persons below a monthly income of Rs 22,500 and subsidised assistance up to Rs 30,000?
x: The ADIP scheme provides free aids and appliances to persons below the stated income limit and subsidised assistance up to Rs 30,000.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: PM-DAKSH — skill training and job linkage
IGNDPS — monthly pension to severely disabled persons from BPL households
SIPDA — free aids and appliances below a specified income ceiling
DDRS — grants to NGOs for rehabilitation and vocational training
x: SIPDA provides grant-in-aid for implementing the RPwD Act. Free aids and appliances are associated with ADIP.

s: UDID-based skilling and the Divyangjan Rozgar Setu for jobs are features of which portal introduced in 2023?
x: The PM-DAKSH-DEPwD portal provides UDID-based skilling and the Divyangjan Rozgar Setu for employment opportunities.

s: The PM-DAKSH Portal for Divyangjan comes under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
x: PM-DAKSH, for skilling, training and job listings for Divyangjan, comes under Social Justice and Empowerment, not Minority Affairs.

s: What does the DDRS scheme for persons with disabilities provide?
o: Free aids and appliances to individuals
x: DDRS gives grants to NGOs; ADIP gives aids to individuals.

s: For what does SIPDA provide grant-in-aid?
x: SIPDA is a grant-in-aid scheme to implement the RPwD Act.

s: Which initiative provides a national centralised database and a single identity card for persons with disabilities?
x: UDID gives one national database and ID card for disability benefits; ADIP gives free assistive devices.

s: Which of the following is NOT a service under Samagra Shiksha's inclusive education component for RPwD-listed disabilities?
x: Samagra Shiksha covers assessment, aids, assistive technology and therapy for children with disabilities, not exclusive education of gifted children.

s: What is Divya Kala Shakti?
o: A health-insurance scheme of the National Trust
A cultural showcase of the artistic talent of persons with disabilities
A loan programme for self-employment of persons with disabilities
A programme for appointing legal guardians
x: Divya Kala Shakti showcases the artistic talent of persons with disabilities and is associated with the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding inclusive education for children with disabilities in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Inclusive education assistance is Rs 3,500 per child with special needs
AP Samagra Shiksha won the national award for Best State in implementing the RPwD Act for 2024-25
Samagra Shiksha's inclusive component targets exclusive education of gifted children
x: Samagra Shiksha's inclusive component covers assessment, aids, assistive technology and therapy; exclusive education of gifted children is not its target.

s: Who is the target group of special education?
x: The target group for special education is children with disabilities, or CwSN; it is not a programme exclusively for gifted groups.

s: Which body organises the EKAM Fest for Divyangjan entrepreneurs?
x: EKAM Fest (Entrepreneurship, Knowledge, Awareness, Marketing) is organised by NDFDC.

s: Which group is the target of the Inclusive India initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the National Trust?
o: Persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities
x: Inclusive India aims to bring persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities into the mainstream.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Initiative)
A. Inclusive India
B. EKAM Fest
C. Divya Kala Shakti
List-II (Purpose)
1. Cultural showcase of the artistic talent of PwDs
2. Entrepreneurship among Divyangjan
3. Mainstreaming persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Inclusive India mainstreams persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities, EKAM Fest promotes entrepreneurship and Divya Kala Shakti showcases artistic talent.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. India ratified the UNCRPD.
B. The UN General Assembly adopted the UNCRPD.
C. The RPwD Act, 2016, was enacted.
D. The RPwD Act, 2016, came into force.
x: The UNCRPD was adopted on 13 December 2006, India ratified it in October 2007, the RPwD Act was enacted in 2016, and it came into force on 19 April 2017.

s: In which year was the International Year of Disabled Persons observed?
x: The International Year of Disabled Persons was observed in 1981.

s: The rights-based RPwD Act, 2016 replaced which welfare-based law?
o: PwD (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995
x: The 2016 Act replaced the welfare-based PwD Act, 1995 with a rights-based framework.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995 – First comprehensive disability law
Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 – Rights-based disability framework
National Trust Act, 1999 – Welfare of persons with autism and cerebral palsy
Rehabilitation Council of India Act, 1992 – Welfare of persons with autism and cerebral palsy
x: The RCI Act, 1992 covers training of rehabilitation professionals; autism and cerebral palsy come under the National Trust Act, 1999.

s: Which committee drafted the initial replacement bill for the PwD Act, 1995, aligning India’s domestic legal architecture with the UNCRPD?
x: The Sudha Kaul Committee (2010) drafted the bill to replace the PwD Act, 1995, in line with the UN disability convention (UNCRPD). This led to the RPwD Act, 2016.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: First National Policy for Persons with Disabilities – 1999
First Chief Commissioner for Disabilities – PWD Act, 1995
National Trust Act for autism, cerebral palsy and related conditions – 1999
Constitutional basis for disability welfare – DPSPs and equality provisions
x: The first National Policy for Persons with Disabilities came in 2006; 1999 is the year of the National Trust Act.

s: The National Trust Act, 1999 covers autism, cerebral palsy, mental retardation and which other condition?
x: The National Trust Act covers autism, cerebral palsy, mental retardation and multiple disabilities.

s: In which year was India's first National Policy for Persons with Disabilities adopted?
x: India's first National Policy for PwDs came in 2006.

s: Under Section 2(s) of the RPwD Act, 2016, a person with disability is one having which kind of long-term impairment?
o: Physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders full and effective participation
Sensory impairment certified exclusively by a Central institution
Physical impairment only, irrespective of social or environmental barriers
Temporary illness that prevents employment for more than six months
x: Section 2(s) covers long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders full participation in society.

s: The RPwD Act, 2016 raised the number of specified disabilities from 7 to how many?
x: The Act raised specified disabilities from 7 to 21, including autism, acid attack victims and sickle cell disease, and lets the Centre add more.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016?
o: It increased specified disabilities from 7 to 21
Benchmark disability means at least 40% of a specified disability
Children with benchmark disabilities get free education from 6 to 18 years
It provides 5% reservation in government jobs and 4% in higher education seats
x: The figures are reversed: the Act gives 4% reservation in government jobs and 5% in higher education.

s: How were survivors of forcible acid ingestion recognised as acid attack victims under the RPwD Act?
o: The adoption of the UNCRPD in 2006
The enactment of the National Trust Act in 1999
The ratification of the UNCRPD by India in 2007
x: After a Supreme Court interpretation in 2026, survivors of forcible acid ingestion were recognised as acid attack victims under the Act.

s: On which date did the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 come into force?
x: The RPwD Act was passed in 2016 and came into force on 19 April 2017.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RPwD Act, 2016:
1. It reserves 4% of government jobs.
2. It reserves 5% of seats in higher education.
3. Benchmark disability means at least 50% disability.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: benchmark disability is at least 40%.

s: Under the RPwD Act, 2016, between which ages do children with benchmark disabilities get free education?
x: The RPwD Act gives free education to benchmark-disability children aged 6–18.

s: Which body maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register?
o: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
x: The Rehabilitation Council of India maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register; the National Trust covers autism, cerebral palsy and related conditions.

s: Which of the following bodies is a statutory authority under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, empowered to monitor implementation and take up complaints?
o: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
x: The Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities is the statutory authority under the RPwD Act, 2016, responsible for monitoring implementation and taking up complaints.

s: Where is SVNIRTAR, a national institute for persons with disabilities, located?
x: SVNIRTAR is at Cuttack; Dehradun hosts the visual-disability institute and NIEPID is at Secunderabad.

s: What does Niramaya, a scheme of the National Trust, provide?
o: Five per cent reservation in higher education
Health insurance up to Rs. 1 lakh per year
x: Niramaya provides health insurance coverage of up to Rs. 1 lakh per year. Travel concessions and loans are associated with other initiatives or institutions.

s: What is the main function of the Rehabilitation Council of India?
o: Provide legal guardianship under the National Trust Act
Monitor implementation of the RPwD Act through State Commissioners
Regulate the training of rehabilitation and special-education professionals and maintain the Central Rehabilitation Register
x: The Rehabilitation Council of India regulates training of rehabilitation and special-education professionals and maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register.

s: Which ministry deals with persons with disabilities?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: Social Justice and Empowerment handles persons with disabilities, through its Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.

s: With what is NHFDC, now the National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation, mainly concerned?
o: Legal guardianship for persons with multiple disabilities
Concessional loans for self-employment of persons with disabilities
x: NHFDC, now NDFDC, provides concessional loans to persons with disabilities for self-employment. It functions under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.

s: Which of the following correctly describes ALIMCO?
o: A statutory authority that monitors implementation of the RPwD Act
A National Trust scheme providing health insurance
A corporation that gives concessional loans for self-employment of Divyangjan
A Central Public Sector Enterprise set up in 1972 that makes aids and artificial limbs
x: ALIMCO is a Central Public Sector Enterprise established in 1972 that manufactures aids and artificial limbs; the other descriptions fit the Chief Commissioner, Niramaya and NDFDC.

s: Which of the following institute–place pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: National institute for visual disability – Dehradun
National institute for locomotor disability – Secunderabad
x: The locomotor disability institute is at Kolkata; NIEPID (intellectual disabilities) is at Secunderabad.

s: Where is NIEPID, the national institute for persons with intellectual disabilities, located?
x: NIEPID is at Secunderabad; SVNIRTAR is at Cuttack and the visual-disability institute at Dehradun.

s: Which body provides legal guardians for persons with autism, cerebral palsy and intellectual disabilities?
x: The National Trust (1999 Act) appoints legal guardians and runs schemes like Niramaya.

s: According to Census 2011, what share of India's population were persons with disabilities?
x: Census 2011 put it at 2.21%, against a global estimate of about 16%, suggesting under-reporting.

s: Which was the largest disability group in India as per Census 2011?
x: Movement disability was the largest among the cited categories at 20.3 percent, followed by hearing at 18.9 percent and seeing at 18.8 percent.

s: What does Andhra Pradesh's Divyang Shakti (2026) provide to persons with disabilities?
x: Divyang Shakti gives 100% free APSRTC bus travel to persons with disabilities; concessional self-employment loans are associated with NDFDC.

s: According to Census 2011, Andhra Pradesh had about how many persons with disabilities?
x: AP had 11.04 lakh persons with disabilities in Census 2011, largely orthopaedic.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's monthly pension for persons with disabilities?
x: AP pays ₹6,000 a month.

s: Which of the following conditions is NOT added to the disability list of Census 2027?
x: Census 2027 adds acid attack, neurological and blood disorders, but autism and dwarfism are left out.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh body provides aids, appliances and economic rehabilitation to persons with disabilities?
o: AP Differently Abled and Senior Citizens Assistance Corporation
x: The AP Differently Abled and Senior Citizens Assistance Corporation provides aids, appliances and economic rehabilitation.

s: Against the Census 2011 figure of 2.21 per cent, about what share of people does the WHO estimate live with disability?
x: The WHO estimates about 16 per cent, which shows under-reporting in the Census.

s: In which List and Entry of the Seventh Schedule is 'Relief of the disabled and unemployable' placed?
x: State List Entry 9 concerns relief of the disabled and unemployable; Article 41 covers public assistance in disablement.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for public assistance in cases of disablement?
x: Article 41 (DPSP) provides public assistance in disablement; Article 46 concerns weaker sections.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UNCRPD?
o: The UN General Assembly adopted it on 13 December 2006
India has ratified its Optional Protocol
Its Optional Protocol provides an individual complaints mechanism
x: The Optional Protocol provides individual complaints, but India has not ratified it.

s: Since which year has the International Day of Persons with Disabilities been observed on 3 December?
x: It has been observed since 1992; 1981 was the International Year of Disabled Persons.

s: With which country did India's Union Cabinet approve a disability-sector MoU in April 2022?
x: The Cabinet approved a DEPwD MoU with Chile in April 2022 and one with South Africa in February 2023.

s: With which country did India approve a disability-sector MoU in February 2023 that covers assistive devices?
x: The February 2023 MoU on disability, including assistive devices, was with South Africa.

s: In line with which law did the Supreme Court direct that prison manuals be revised for accessibility of prisoners with disabilities?
o: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
The Rehabilitation Council of India Act, 1992
x: The Supreme Court directed prison accessibility and revision of prison manuals in accordance with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.

s: The Supreme Court recognised safe footpaths as a fundamental right under which Article, along with a minimum footpath width of 1.8 metres?
x: The Supreme Court recognised safe footpaths as part of the right to life under Article 21 and specified a minimum width of 1.8 metres.

s: The Supreme Court’s recognition of digital access as part of Article 21 was made with reference to which international convention?
o: Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women
United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child
x: The Supreme Court recognised digital access as part of Article 21 while citing the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.

s: In March 2026, what did the Supreme Court hold about the 40% threshold for benchmark disability?
o: Ceiling applicable only to Group A posts
Limit applicable only to locomotor disability
x: The Court treated 40% as a floor, not a ceiling, with suitability judged by functional ability and reasonable accommodation.

s: Which case held that the scribe facility cannot be restricted only to persons with benchmark disabilities?
o: Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India
Disabled Rights Group v. Union of India
Rajive Raturi v. Union of India
x: Vikash Kumar v. UPSC (2021) treated reasonable accommodation as part of equality, so scribes cannot be limited to benchmark disabilities.

s: Which case dealt with the deplaning of a woman with cerebral palsy and her right to dignity?
o: Rajive Raturi v. Union of India
Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India
x: Jeeja Ghosh concerned deplaning and dignity; mandatory accessibility standards were the issue in Rajive Raturi.

s: With which of the following is Rajive Raturi v. Union of India associated?
o: Time-bound accessibility directions for public transport and buildings
Deplaning of a passenger with cerebral palsy
x: Rajive Raturi gave time-bound accessibility directions for built infrastructure and public transport, not limited to any one kind of institution.

s: Which ministry administers IGNOAPS, a component of the National Social Assistance Programme?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: IGNOAPS is under NSAP and the Ministry of Rural Development; its assistance has been frozen at Rs 200 since 2007.

s:
Consider the following statements about IGNOAPS:
1. It is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development.
2. The Centre's share has been revised every year since 2007.
3. It pays Rs 200 a month to those aged 60-79 and Rs 500 to those aged 80 and above.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Centre's share has been frozen at Rs 200 since 2007.

s: When was the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) launched?
x: NSAP was launched on 15 August 1995 under the Ministry of Rural Development.

s: Under the Annapurna component of NSAP, how much free food grain do eligible seniors not getting IGNOAPS receive?
x: Annapurna gives 10 kg of free food grains a month to seniors eligible for, but not receiving, IGNOAPS.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NSAP components?
o: NFBS is a component of Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana
IGNDPS covers persons with 80% or more disability
NFBS gives a lump sum of Rs 20,000 on the death of the primary breadwinner
x: NFBS is a component of NSAP, not AVYAY; the other three statements are correct.

s: Which State runs the Mukhyamantri Vriddhajan Pension Yojana, a universal old-age pension with no income bar?
x: Bihar's Mukhyamantri Vriddhajan Pension Yojana (2019) covers all aged 60+ without another pension: Rs 400 (60-79), Rs 500 (80+).

s: To what amount did Andhra Pradesh raise the NTR Bharosa old-age pension in June 2024 (G.O. 43)?
x: The NTR Bharosa old-age pension was raised from Rs 3,000 to Rs 4,000 a month on 13 June 2024.

s: What is the minimum age for old-age pension for ST beneficiaries under the NTR Bharosa Pension?
x: The minimum age is 60 years in general, but 50 years for ST beneficiaries.

s: What was the earlier name of Andhra Pradesh's NTR Bharosa Pension scheme?
x: The NTR Bharosa Pension was earlier called YSR Pension Kanuka.

s: From which fund is the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana for BPL senior citizens financed?
x: The scheme is funded from the Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund and requires at least 30 per cent women beneficiaries in each district.

s: Under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPOP), a component of AVYAY, eligible NGOs may get up to what share of project cost?
x: IPOP can fund up to 90 per cent of project cost for old-age homes, day-care centres and mobile medicare units.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the components of Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana?
x: The four components of AVYAY are the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens, State Action Plan, Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana and Elder Line. The National Family Benefit Scheme is an NSAP component.

s: For whom is the Ayushman Vay Vandana card under AB-PMJAY meant?
o: Children below 10 years from SECC households
Only women aged 70 years and above
All persons aged 60 years and above subject to an income ceiling
All persons aged 70 years and above irrespective of income
x: All senior citizens aged 70 years and above are eligible for the Ayushman Vay Vandana card irrespective of income.

s: Which ministry and agency implement the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana?
x: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana is associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and ALIMCO.

s: What assured pension did the Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana offer when it was launched in 2017?
x: PMVVY offered an assured pension of 8% for 10 years, with a maximum purchase price of Rs 7.5 lakh and maximum pension of Rs 5,000 a month.

s: How much health cover does the Ayushman Vay Vandana card provide?
x: The Ayushman Vay Vandana card (AB-PMJAY, 2024) gives Rs 5 lakh health cover to all aged 70+, irrespective of income.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: IGNOAPS – Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: PMVVY is a pension scheme run through LIC. Vayoshri is run with ALIMCO, Vay Vandana is under AB-PMJAY and IGNOAPS is under MoRD.

s: Under SAGE (Seniorcare Ageing Growth Engine), how much equity support can elder-care start-ups get?
x: SAGE, under AVYAY, offers up to Rs 1 crore equity for elder-care start-ups, with the Government's stake below 49%.

s: Where was the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana launched on 1 April 2017?
x: The Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana was launched at Nellore in Andhra Pradesh on 1 April 2017.

s: Which of the following is given free to BPL senior citizens under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana?
o: Physical aids such as walking sticks, wheelchairs and hearing aids
10 kg of food grains a month
x: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana gives free physical aids like walking sticks, wheelchairs, hearing aids and dentures to BPL seniors through ALIMCO.

s: Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), launched in April 2021, was renamed from which earlier scheme?
o: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly
National Action Plan for Senior Citizens
x: AVYAY was formed in April 2021 by renaming the National Action Plan for Senior Citizens.

s: What was the maximum purchase limit under the Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana after its revision in 2018?
x: PMVVY's maximum purchase limit was Rs 7.5 lakh at launch and was raised to Rs 15 lakh in 2018.

s: Under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, at least what share of beneficiaries in each district must be women?
x: The Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana requires that at least 30% of beneficiaries in each district are women.

s: Which ministry runs the Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY)?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: PMVVY is a Ministry of Finance pension scheme run through LIC; it closed for new subscription after 31 March 2023.

s: Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, on whom does the obligation to maintain parents fall?
o: Only biological sons above 18 years of age
Biological, adopted and step-children, and legal heirs in the relevant circumstances
x: The Act places obligations on biological, adopted and step-children, and also on legal heirs in relation to senior citizens who cannot maintain themselves.

s: What does Section 20 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 deal with?
x: Section 20 concerns the provision of medical care for senior citizens and forms the basis of the National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007?
o: Its 2019 Amendment Bill, removing the maintenance ceiling, was enacted by Parliament
Abandoning a senior citizen may attract imprisonment up to three months and/or a fine up to ₹5,000
At least one old-age home is contemplated in every district
It is administered by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The 2019 Amendment Bill proposed removing the maintenance cap but was not passed.

s: Which provision lets the Tribunal declare void a senior citizen's property transfer when the transferee fails to provide the promised care?
o: Section 12 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
Section 20 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
Section 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
Section 32 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
x: Section 23 of the 2007 Act permits the Tribunal to declare such a transfer void when the promised basic needs and care are not provided.

s: Which was the first State to enact a law for the maintenance of parents, before the central Act of 2007?
x: Himachal Pradesh enacted the Maintenance of Parents and Dependents Act, 2001, the first such State law. Kerala is first with a Senior Citizens' Welfare Department; Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka are not cited as first.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, who heads the Maintenance Tribunal at the sub-divisional level under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007?
x: In Andhra Pradesh, the Maintenance Tribunal functions at the sub-division level and is headed by the Revenue Divisional Officer or Sub-Collector.

s: Which one of the following is a correct provision of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007?
o: The Maintenance Tribunal can decide only cases relating to property transfer.
The Maintenance Tribunal has no power to permit an appeal.
The Maintenance Tribunal may award up to Rs 20,000 per month and should decide the case within 30 days.
The Maintenance Tribunal may award up to Rs 10,000 per month and should decide the case within 90 days.
x: The Act prescribed a maximum maintenance of Rs 10,000 per month, required disposal within 90 days and allowed an appeal.

s: How was the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 brought into force?
o: On one date for all States, 29 December 2007
On one date for all States, 1 January 2008
Only in Union Territories from 29 December 2007
x: The Act was brought into force state by state from 29 December 2007, not on a single date for all States.

s: What happened to the Senior Citizens (Amendment) Bill, 2019, which proposed covering in-laws and grandchildren?
o: It was enacted as an Act in 2019
It was enacted as an Act in 2021
It was passed by Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha in 2020
x: The 2019 Bill proposed removing the Rs 10,000 cap and covering in-laws and grandchildren, but it was not passed.

s: Under the Senior Citizens Act, 2007, what is the maximum punishment for abandoning a senior citizen?
x: Abandoning a senior citizen attracts up to 3 months' jail and/or a Rs 5,000 fine.

s: Under the Senior Citizens Act, 2007, how many old age homes must be set up at minimum?
x: The Act requires at least one old age home in every district.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, who heads the Appellate Tribunal under the Senior Citizens Act, 2007?
x: The Appellate Tribunal works at district level under the District Collector; the Maintenance Tribunal is at sub-division level under the RDO/Sub-Collector.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Senior Citizens Act, 2007:
1. The maximum maintenance is Rs 10,000 per month.
2. A maintenance case must be decided within 90 days.
3. The duty to maintain parents falls only on biological children.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: biological, adopted and step-children and legal heirs must maintain parents.

s: Which Section of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 is the basis of the National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly (NPHCE)?
x: Section 20 of the Act deals with medical care of senior citizens and is the basis of the NPHCE.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly – 1999
Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act – 2007
x: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act dates to 2007; NPOP is 1999, NPHCE began in 2010–11 and NPSC is 2011.

s: Under the National Policy on Older Persons, 1999, from what age is a person treated as an 'older person'?
x: The National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 defines an older person as an individual aged 60 years or above.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about policies for the elderly?
o: The National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 was framed by MoSJE
The National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011 gives special focus to elderly women
The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly was launched by MoSJE
The National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011 emphasises ageing in place
x: NPHCE was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 2010-11, not MoSJE.

s: Which concept is a focus of the National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011?
o: Institutionalisation of all elderly in old age homes
Welfare only for elderly in joint families
x: NPSC 2011 focuses on ageing in place, along with income security, homecare, health insurance and harsh punishment for elder abuse.

s: Which ministry runs the National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly (NPHCE), 2010-11?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: NPHCE belongs to MoHFW, not MoSJE; Section 20 of the 2007 Act on medical care is its basis.

s: How many principal areas of intervention did the National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 identify?
x: NPOP 1999 (MoSJE) defined an older person as 60+ and listed 14 principal areas of intervention, including health care and nutrition.

s: What is the number of Elder Line, the National Helpline for Senior Citizens under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment?
x: Elder Line 14567 is the National Helpline for Senior Citizens, operated under MoSJE; it is not limited to pension disbursement.

s: Elder Line 14567 is a component of which scheme?
x: Elder Line is one of the four components of AVYAY, along with IPSrC, State Action Plan and RVY.

s: Who provides technical support for Elder Line?
x: Elder Line, under MoSJE, gets technical support from Tata Trusts and NSE Foundation and runs with State emergency response centres.

s: Which institution conducted Wave 1 of the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI)?
x: LASI Wave 1 (2017-18) was conducted by IIPS, Mumbai under MoHFW; its report was released in 2021.

s: According to the India Ageing Report 2023, by which year will the elderly outnumber children (0-14)?
x: The UNFPA–IIPS India Ageing Report 2023 projects the elderly to exceed children aged 0-14 by 2046.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the India Ageing Report 2023?
o: It was prepared by HelpAge India
It was prepared by UNFPA with IIPS
It flags feminisation of ageing as a key challenge
It flags ruralisation of ageing as a key challenge
x: The report was prepared by UNFPA with IIPS, not HelpAge India; feminisation and ruralisation are among its key challenges.

s: LASI Wave 1 covered persons of which age group and their spouses?
x: LASI covered about 72,250 persons aged 45+ and their spouses.

s: As per the NSO report 'Elderly in India 2021', about what share of Andhra Pradesh's population was aged 60 years and above in 2021?
x: The NSO report projected 12.4% of Andhra Pradesh's population to be 60+ in 2021, above the national 10.1%; Kerala was highest at 16.5%.

s: Which organisation is associated with elderly-care services and the release of elder-abuse surveys in India?
x: HelpAge India runs elderly-care services and releases surveys relating to elder abuse.

s: Who among the following is known as the first voter of independent India?
x: Shyam Saran Negi of Kalpa, Kinnaur (Himachal Pradesh) cast the first vote of independent India in October 1951.

s: The UN Decade of Healthy Ageing covers which period?
x: The UN Decade of Healthy Ageing covers the period 2021–2030.

s: On which date is the International Day of Older Persons observed?
x: The International Day of Older Persons is observed on 1 October.

s: On which date is World Elder Abuse Awareness Day observed?
x: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day is observed on 15 June.

s: The Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing was adopted in which year?
x: The Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing dates to 2002. 1999 is India's NPOP, 2011 is India's NPSC, and 2021 is the start of the UN Decade of Healthy Ageing (2021-2030).

s: In the history of India's population growth, what is the year 1921 known as?
o: Start of high but slowing growth
x: 1921 is called the Great Divide: population declined in 1911-21 and grew steadily after 1921. The explosion phase was 1951-81 (over 2% a year), and 1981-2011 saw high but slowing growth.

s: What was India's decadal population growth rate for 2001-11 as per Census 2011?
x: Decadal growth in 2001-11 was 17.7%; India's population was about 121.09 crore, 68.9% of it rural.

s: As per Census 2011, what share of India's population was rural?
x: Census 2011 counted about 121.09 crore people, 68.9% of them rural.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's approximate share of India's population (2025-26)?
x: AP has 495.77 lakh people, about 4.09% of India, ranking 10th.

s: Which State had the highest sex ratio as per Census 2011?
x: Kerala had the highest sex ratio in Census 2011 at 1084 females per 1000 males.

s: What was India's sex ratio as per Census 2011?
x: Census 2011 recorded India's sex ratio as 943 females per 1000 males.

s: Which State recorded the lowest sex ratio in Census 2011?
x: Haryana had the lowest sex ratio among States in Census 2011 at 879.

s: In which Census did agricultural labourers outnumber cultivators in India for the first time?
x: Census 2011 showed that the number of cultivators fell and agricultural labourers outnumbered cultivators for the first time.

s: Which period of India's population growth is known as the phase of population explosion?
x: From 1951 to 1981 India's population grew at over 2% a year, so this period is called the population explosion phase.

s: Which State recorded the highest decadal population growth during 1991-2001?
x: Nagaland recorded the highest decadal growth (about 64%) in 1991-2001, while Kerala recorded the lowest.

s: Which was the second most populous State of India as per Census 2011?
x: In Census 2011 the order was Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and then West Bengal.

s: Census 2011 was which Census of India in the series?
x: Census 2011 was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after Independence.

s: Which State recorded the highest decadal population growth during 2001-11, when Nagaland recorded negative growth?
x: In 2001-11 Meghalaya had the highest decadal growth among States, while Nagaland's growth was negative.

s: What was India's work participation rate as per Census 2011?
x: Census 2011 recorded a work participation rate of 39.8% (about 482 million workers); the female rate was about 25.5%.

s: Which State had the highest share of Hindus in its population as per Census 2011?
x: Himachal Pradesh had the highest Hindu share (about 95%) in Census 2011; Hindus were 79.8% of India.

s: In which year is the next Census of India due?
x: The next Census of India is due in 2027.

s: In which year did T.R. Malthus publish 'An Essay on the Principle of Population'?
x: Malthus's Essay on the Principle of Population appeared in 1798.

s: According to Malthus, in which progression does food supply grow?
x: Malthus held that food grows in arithmetic progression (1, 2, 3, 4) while population grows in geometric progression (1, 2, 4, 8).

s: In Malthusian theory, what type of check is moral restraint such as late marriage and celibacy?
x: Preventive checks lower the birth rate (moral restraint); positive checks such as famine and war raise the death rate.

s: Who propounded the theory of optimum population?
x: Edwin Cannan gave the optimum population theory and rejected Malthus's view of an inherent tendency to overpopulation.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Demographic transition theory – Warren Thompson and Frank Notestein
x: Demographic transition theory is linked to Thompson and Notestein. Optimum population is Cannan's; late marriage is a preventive check and famine a positive check.

s: Which sequence correctly represents the stages of demographic transition?
o: Both rates low → birth rate falls → death rate falls → high rates
High birth and death rates → death rate falls → birth rate falls → both rates low
High birth and death rates → birth rate falls → death rate rises → both rates high
Death rate falls → both rates low → birth rate rises → high death rate
x: The demographic transition proceeds from high birth and death rates, to falling death rates, then falling birth rates, and finally low birth and death rates.

s: In which stage of demographic transition is India presently described as being?
x: India is described as being in the youth-bulge stage of demographic transition.

s: The dependency ratio is calculated by which of the following formulas?
x: The dependency ratio is calculated as the population aged 0–14 plus the population aged 65 and above, divided by the population aged 15–64.

s: Till about which year is India's demographic dividend window expected to last?
x: India's demographic dividend window, from a rising working-age share, lasts till about 2055.

s: According to NFHS-5, which of the following correctly represents the total fertility rate of India and Andhra Pradesh?
x: NFHS-5 recorded India’s total fertility rate at 2.0 and Andhra Pradesh’s at 1.7.

s: According to SRS 2024, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: India’s TFR was 2.4, with rural and urban rates equal.
India’s TFR was 2.1 and urban TFR was higher than rural TFR.
India’s TFR was 1.5, with rural TFR at 1.9 and urban TFR at 2.1.
India’s TFR was 1.9, with rural TFR at 2.1 and urban TFR at 1.5.
x: SRS 2024 reported India’s TFR at 1.9, rural TFR at 2.1 and urban TFR at 1.5.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about fertility as per SRS 2024?
o: India's TFR has stayed below 2.1 for the fifth year
Delhi has the lowest TFR at 1.2
Bihar has the lowest TFR among States
x: Bihar is the highest-fertility State, not the lowest; Delhi (1.2) has the lowest TFR.

s: Which State had the highest total fertility rate (TFR) as per NFHS-5?
x: NFHS-5 (2019-21) recorded Bihar's TFR as 3.0, the highest among States.

s: In which year did India launch the world's first national family planning programme?
x: India was the first country to launch a national family planning programme, in 1952.

s: India's early family planning programme had little rural impact mainly because it was:
x: The early approach was clinic-based and concentrated in cities, so it reached few rural people.

s: The shift from population control to individual well-being and reproductive health followed which conference?
x: The ICPD at Cairo in 1994 moved the focus from population control to individual well-being and reproductive health.

s: When did India adopt the target-free approach in family planning, dropping method-specific contraceptive targets?
x: In April 1996 India dropped method-specific contraceptive targets and adopted a target-free approach.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Population Policy 2000:
1. Its long-term objective is a stable population by 2050.
2. Its immediate objective is to meet the unmet need for contraception.
3. Its medium-term objective is to reach TFR 2.1 by 2010.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the long-term goal is a stable population by 2045.

s: Who chairs the National Commission on Population, set up in May 2000?
x: The Commission is chaired by the Prime Minister, with the Chief Ministers of all States/UTs as members.

s: About how many new working-age people does India need jobs for every year?
x: About 9.7 million new working-age people enter each year; the demographic dividend pays off only if they are employed.

s: Which effect of population growth on land is commonly cited?
x: Population growth puts pressure on resources and leads to smaller land holdings.

s: What weight does population carry in Finance Commission formulas?
x: Population carries 15–25% weight in Finance Commission formulas, which is why southern States that controlled population fear losing out.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: India – First national family planning programme
Kerala – First Senior Citizens' Welfare Department
Andhra Pradesh – Draft Population Management Policy
x: The draft Population Management Policy is associated with Andhra Pradesh; Kerala was first with the senior-citizens framework.

s: What did the Supreme Court decide in Javed v. State of Haryana (2003)?
o: Abolished two-child norms for local elections across India
Ruled only on the dependency ratio
x: In Javed v. State of Haryana (2003), the Supreme Court upheld Haryana's two-child norm.

s: From which year did Andhra Pradesh's two-child norm for local body elections, removed by Bills in 2024, date?
x: AP's two-child norm for local polls dated from 1994; the AP Panchayat Raj and Municipal Laws (Amendment) Bills, 2024 removed it.

s: AP's draft Population Management Policy (March 2026) offers an incentive of what amount for a second or third child?
x: The draft policy moves from control to management and offers Rs 25,000 for a second or third child.

s: Which of the following is a feature of Andhra Pradesh's draft Population Management Policy (March 2026)?
o: A two-child norm for contesting local body elections
Incentives for a second or third child, marking a shift from population control to population management
A cash penalty on families with more than two children
Compulsory sterilisation after the second child
x: The March 2026 draft policy moves from population control to population management and offers incentives (Rs 25,000) for a second or third child. A two-child norm, penalties or sterilisation would be control measures, the opposite of the policy.

s: At whose request did the Institute for Competitiveness prepare the Quality of Life for Elderly Index (2021)?
x: The Institute for Competitiveness prepared the index at the request of the Economic Advisory Council to the PM.

s: Under the Quality of Life for Elderly Index (2021), which category–top performer pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Chandigarh topped the Union Territories, not Delhi; the other pairs are correct.

s: When was Wave 1 of the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI) conducted?
x: LASI Wave 1 was conducted in 2017-18 by IIPS for MoHFW and released in 2021.

s:
Consider the following statements about the elderly (60+) population in 2021, as per the NSO report 'Elderly in India 2021':
1. Andhra Pradesh's elderly share (about 12.4%) was above the national average.
2. Kerala had the highest elderly share among States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Andhra Pradesh's elderly share was about 12.4% against India's 10.1%, and Kerala led with 16.5%.

s: Under which programme can NGOs receive support of up to 90% of the cost of old age homes?
o: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly
x: The Integrated Programme for Older Persons provides NGOs with support of up to 90% of the costs of old age homes.

s: About what percentage of elderly persons in India have no pension?
x: About 78% of the elderly have no pension and about 70% depend on others.

s: The National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011 drew attention to destitution among which group?
o: Elderly persons in old age homes
x: NPSC 2011 backed 'ageing in place' and highlighted destitution among the rural elderly.

s: The elderly account for about what share of hospitalisation spending in India?
x: The elderly account for about 30–35% of hospitalisation spending; ageing does not remove the need for long-term health expenditure.

s: Which State is the first in India to have a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget?
x: Kerala is the first State to establish all three: a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget.

s: In which year was the National Policy on Older Persons (NPOP) announced?
x: The National Policy on Older Persons was announced in 1999. NPSC came in 2011, while 2007 is the year of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act.

s: About what percentage of the elderly in India depend on others?
x: About 70% of the elderly depend on others; 78% have no pension.

s: What is the presence of more elderly women, especially widows, among the aged population called?
x: Feminisation of ageing refers to the growing share of women, many of them widows, among the elderly.

s: Transgender persons have demanded which type of reservation, cutting across SC, ST, OBC and General categories?
o: Reservation only under the women's quota
x: The community seeks horizontal reservation across SC, ST, OBC and General; NALSA's SEBC treatment resembled a vertical OBC-type quota.

s: Which State was the first to formulate a transgender policy?
x: Kerala was the first State to formulate a transgender policy, in 2015.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State measures for transgender persons?
o: Tamil Nadu set up a Transgender Welfare Board in 2008
The Thirunangaigal app was launched in 2021
The Thirunangaigal app for ID registration is a Kerala measure
Sthree Suraksha for EWS women and transgender persons is a Kerala scheme
x: The Thirunangaigal app (2021) is a Tamil Nadu measure, not a Kerala one.

s: The issue of reservation for transgender persons resurfaced in June 2023 in connection with which State?
x: The issue resurfaced through a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra’s reply to the Bombay High Court in June 2023.

s: What percentage of reservation in all government services did Karnataka provide for transgender persons in July 2021?
x: In July 2021 Karnataka became the first State to give 1% reservation to transgender persons in all government services.

s: Which State was the first to set up a Transgender Welfare Board, in 2008?
x: Tamil Nadu set up the Transgender Welfare Board in 2008; Karnataka gave the first job quota and Kerala framed the first policy.

s: Andhra Pradesh has issued about how many transgender certificates via the National Portal?
x: AP has issued about 3,125 certificates via the National Portal and has a State Transgender Policy 2025.

s: In which year did Andhra Pradesh bring out its State Transgender Policy?
x: Andhra Pradesh has a State Transgender Policy of 2025; Kerala's 2015 policy was the first in India.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: K. Prithika Yashini – First transgender judge
Manabi Bandyopadhyay – First transgender college principal
Madhu Bai Kinnar – First transgender college principal
x: Manabi Bandyopadhyay became the first transgender college principal in 2015. Joyita Mondal was the first transgender judge, Prithika Yashini the first police sub-inspector and Madhu Bai Kinnar the first mayor.

s: Laxmi Narayan Tripathi was the first transgender person from the Asia-Pacific to:
x: Laxmi Narayan Tripathi was the first from the Asia-Pacific to address the UN General Assembly.

s: Who became India's first openly transgender mayor, in Raigarh, Chhattisgarh, in 2015?
x: Madhu Bai Kinnar became the first openly transgender mayor at Raigarh in 2015.

s: Who was India's first transgender police sub-inspector?
x: K. Prithika Yashini of Tamil Nadu became the first transgender police sub-inspector.

s: Who became India's first transgender MLA, in Madhya Pradesh in 1998?
x: Shabnam Mausi became the first transgender MLA (MP, 1998); Madhu Bai Kinnar was the first transgender mayor (Raigarh, 2015).

s: On which date was NALSA v. Union of India delivered?
x: NALSA was delivered on 15 April 2014 by Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri.

s: According to NALSA v. Union of India, how is a person's gender identity determined?
x: NALSA held that gender identity is self-determined, not dependent on biology or State verification.

s: Which of the following was a direction of the Supreme Court in NALSA v. Union of India?
o: Certificate on a medical board's recommendation
Separate public toilets and health facilities
x: NALSA directed separate public toilets, health facilities and welfare schemes, and SEBC treatment (a vertical quota).

s: In NALSA v. Union of India (2014), what kind of reservation did the Supreme Court direct for transgender persons?
o: Vertical reservation by treating them as socially and educationally backward classes
x: NALSA directed that transgender persons be treated as SEBCs, giving a vertical, OBC-type quota; the community now demands horizontal reservation.

s: Which judges delivered the NALSA v. Union of India judgment on 15 April 2014?
o: Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri
Justices D.Y. Chandrachud and S.K. Kaul
Justices J.S. Khehar and R.F. Nariman
Justices Dipak Misra and A.M. Khanwilkar
x: The NALSA judgment was delivered by Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court recognise transgender persons as the 'third gender'?
o: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
x: NALSA v. Union of India (2014) recognised transgender persons as the 'third gender' with self-determined gender identity.

s: Which case declared privacy a fundamental right under Article 21?
x: A nine-judge bench in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017) held privacy to be a fundamental right under Article 21.

s: For what is Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018) known?
o: Decriminalising same-sex relations under Section 377 IPC
x: Navtej (2018) decriminalised same-sex relations under Section 377 IPC.

s: What did the five-judge bench decide by a 3:2 majority in Supriyo v. Union of India (October 2023)?
o: Refused legal recognition of same-sex marriage, leaving it to Parliament
x: Supriyo refused legal recognition of same-sex marriage and left the matter to Parliament.

s: How many judges decided K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017), which held privacy to be a fundamental right?
x: A nine-judge bench in Puttaswamy (2017) held privacy to be a fundamental right under Article 21.

s: Garima Greh under SMILE is primarily associated with which service?
x: Garima Greh provides shelter homes for transgender persons.

s: What is the goal of the SMILE scheme, launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in 2022?
x: SMILE, an umbrella Central Sector scheme, aims at a begging-free India, 'Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat'.

s: What is the expanded form of SMILE in the context of welfare schemes?
o: Social Mission for Inclusive Livelihood and Employment
Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise
Scheme for Marginalised Inclusion, Livelihood and Education
Support Mission for Independent Living and Empowerment
x: SMILE stands for Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise.

s: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, how many Garima Greh shelter homes run in how many States/UTs?
x: There are 23 Garima Grehs in 17 States/UTs.

s: What is the outlay of the SMILE umbrella scheme?
x: SMILE (2022, MoSJE) is a Central Sector umbrella scheme with an outlay of Rs 365 crore.

s: Through which scheme is skilling given to transgender persons under SMILE?
x: SMILE's rehabilitation component provides skilling through PM-DAKSH, along with scholarships and a PM-JAY health package.

s: Under the NTR Bharosa Pension scheme in Andhra Pradesh, what is the monthly pension for elderly persons aged 60 years and above, widows and transgender persons?
x: NTR Bharosa provides Rs 4,000 per month to elderly persons aged 60 years and above, widows and transgender persons.

s: According to Census 2011, approximately how many transgender persons were counted in India?
x: Census 2011 counted approximately 4.88 lakh transgender persons in India.

s: As per Census 2011, which State had the highest number of transgender persons?
x: Census 2011 counted about 4.88 lakh transgender persons, the most in Uttar Pradesh, followed by undivided AP.

s: Who moved the Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 as a private member's Bill?
x: The Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 was moved as a private member's Bill by Tiruchi Siva of the DMK.

s: When did the Rajya Sabha pass the Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014, a private member's Bill?
x: It passed the Rajya Sabha in April 2015, the first private member's Bill passed there in over four decades, but was not passed by the Lok Sabha.

s: Why is the Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014, passed by the Rajya Sabha in April 2015, significant?
o: It was the first Bill on transgender rights to become law
It was the first private member's Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha in over four decades
It was the first Bill passed at a joint sitting of Parliament
It was the first Government Bill on gender identity
x: Tiruchi Siva's Bill was the first private member's Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha in over four decades; the Lok Sabha did not pass it.

s: Who introduced the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha on 13 March 2026?
x: Union Social Justice Minister Virendra Kumar introduced the Amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha on 13 March 2026.

s: On what ground has the 2026 amendment to the transgender persons law been mainly criticised?
o: Removing the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court over identity matters
Extending the NALSA principle to old-age pensions
Reversing the self-identification principle recognised in NALSA
Strengthening the self-identification principle of NALSA
x: The principal criticism is that medical certification reverses the self-identification principle associated with the NALSA judgment.

s: Which of the following was a criticism of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019?
o: It prescribed heavier penalties than those for comparable crimes against women.
It completely abolished the role of the District Magistrate in identity certification.
It provided no reservation for transgender persons.
It excluded all socio-cultural transgender identities from its definition.
x: Criticisms included lighter penalties than for similar crimes against women, District Magistrate gatekeeping of identity and the absence of reservation. The Act did include several socio-cultural identities.

s: Under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, who issues the certificate of identity?
x: The District Magistrate issues the certificate (a revised one after surgery); the National Council only advises and monitors policy.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2026 amendment to the transgender persons law?
o: The District Magistrate issues the certificate on the recommendation of a designated medical board
The definition is limited to specified socio-cultural identities, intersex variations and persons forced to present as transgender
Self-perceived identity continues to be expressly included without restriction
Kidnapping and forcing a person to present as transgender were added as offences
x: The amendment excludes self-perceived identity and omits Section 4(2).

s: Whom does the definition of a transgender person under the 2019 Act include?
o: Only persons who have undergone sex reassignment surgery
Only persons certified by a medical board
Only persons of the hijra community
x: The 2019 definition includes persons with intersex variations, trans men and women, genderqueer persons and socio-cultural identities such as kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta.

s: Who challenged the 2026 amendment to the transgender persons law in the Supreme Court?
o: Madhu Bai Kinnar and Shabnam Mausi
Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel
x: Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel challenged the amendment as contrary to the principles laid down in NALSA.

s: Under the 2019 Act, what imprisonment do offences such as forced labour or abuse of transgender persons carry?
x: Offences under the 2019 Act carry 6 months to 2 years plus fine, criticised as lighter than for similar crimes against women.

s: When did the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 come into force?
x: The 2019 Act came into force on 10 January 2020.

s: Under the 2019 Act, when does the District Magistrate issue a revised certificate of identity?
o: After one year of the first certificate
x: The DM issues the certificate of identity and a revised certificate after surgery.

s: The National Council for Transgender Persons is constituted as a statutory body under which legislation?
o: The National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019
x: The National Council for Transgender Persons is a statutory body constituted under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.

s: Which ministry administers the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
